title: What happened
goal: Talk about past events: where you went, what you did, what happened — using the ergative construction correctly.
intro:
The Gujarati past tense has two patterns. With verbs that have **no object** (go, come, sit), the past works like an adjective agreeing with the subject: **હું ગયો** 'I went' (man), **હું ગઈ** (woman).

With verbs that **take an object** (eat, see, say), Gujarati uses the **ergative construction**: the doer gets the ending **-એ** (or a special pronoun form like **મેં** 'I'), and the verb agrees with the **object**, not the doer: **મેં ચા પીધી** 'I drank tea' — પીધી is feminine because ચા is feminine.

vocab.note: X ને મળવું 'to meet X'; મને મળ્યું 'I got (it)'
usually ભૂલી જવું: હું ભૂલી ગયો 'I forgot'
f · મને યાદ છે 'I remember'; યાદ આવ્યું 'I remembered'
ગયા અઠવાડિયે 'last week', ગયા વર્ષે 'last year'

phrases.native: ગયા વર્ષે અમે કચ્છ ગયાં હતાં.
phrases.roman: gayā varṣe ame Kachchh gayāṃ hatāṃ.
phrases.en: Last year we went to Kutch.

grammar.title: Past tense of intransitive verbs: agree with the subject
grammar.body:
The past form is made from the stem + **-યો / -ી / -યું / -યા / -યાં** (like an adjective). With verbs that take no object, it agrees with the **subject**:

હું આવ**્યો** (man) / આવ**ી** (woman) — I came
એ આવ**્યો** / આવ**ી** — he / she came
અમે આવ**્યા** (men or mixed) / આવ**્યાં** (mixed or neuter) — we came
બાળક આવ**્યું** — the child came

Important irregulars: **જવું → ગયો / ગઈ / ગયું**, **થવું → થયો / થઈ / થયું**, **બેસવું → બેઠો**, **સૂવું → સૂતો**, **રહેવું → રહ્યો**.

Negative: add **નહીં** after or **નથી** before: **એ આવ્યો નહીં** / **એ નથી આવ્યો** 'he didn't come / hasn't come'.

grammar.title: The ergative: મેં ચા પીધી
grammar.body:
With **transitive** verbs (verbs with an object), the past tense uses the ergative construction:

1. The **doer takes -એ**: રામ → **રામે**, સીતા → **સીતાએ**, છોકરો → **છોકરાએ**. Pronouns: **મેં** (I), **તેં** (you, intimate), **એણે / તેણે** (he, she), **અમે / આપણે** (we), **તમે** (you), **એમણે / તેમણે** (they; he/she respectful).
2. The **verb agrees with the object**: ચા (f) → **પીધી**; પાણી (n) → **પીધું**; નાસ્તો (m) → **કર્યો**; રોટલી (f pl) → **ખાધી**.

So **મેં ચા પીધી**, **મેં પાણી પીધું**, **સીતાએ નાસ્તો કર્યો** — the verb doesn't care whether the doer is male or female. Unlike Hindi, Gujarati keeps this agreement even when the object has -ને: **મેં સીતાને જોઈ** 'I saw Sita'. With no clear object, use neuter -યું: **તમે શું કહ્યું?**

Key irregular pasts: **ખાવું → ખાધું, પીવું → પીધું, લેવું → લીધું, દેવું → દીધું, કરવું → કર્યું, કહેવું → કહ્યું, જોવું → જોયું**.

examples.en: Sita wrote a letter. (પત્ર is m)
We bought a new house. (ઘર is n)
What did they / did he (resp.) say?

grammar.title: Perfect and past continuous: છે, હતું, -તો હતો
grammar.body:
Add **છે** to the past form for the present perfect ('have done'): **હું આવ્યો છું** 'I have come', **મેં ખાધું છે** 'I have eaten'.

Add **હતું** (agreeing) for the pluperfect or a completed past: **અમે કચ્છ ગયાં હતાં** 'we had gone / went to Kutch'.

For 'was doing' or 'used to do', use the **-તો** form + **હતો**: **હું વાંચતો હતો** 'I was reading / used to read'. Without હતો, the bare -તો form also means 'used to' in storytelling: **અમે રોજ દરિયે જતા** 'we used to go to the sea every day'.

examples.native: જ્યારે ફોન આવ્યો, હું જમતો હતો.
examples.roman: jyāre fon āvyo, huṃ jamto hato.
examples.en: When the phone rang, I was eating.
As a child I used to play cricket.

dialogue.title: Monday morning
dialogue.setting: Colleagues Bhavin and Sarah catch up about the weekend.

lines.speaker: Bhavin
lines.en: Sarah, what did you do at the weekend?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: શનિવારે હું મારી બહેનપણીના લગ્નમાં ગઈ.
lines.roman: shanivāre huṃ mārī bahenpaṇīnā lagnamāṃ gaī.
lines.en: On Saturday I went to my friend's wedding.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: બહુ મજા આવી. મેં પહેલી વાર ગરબા કર્યા!
lines.roman: bahu majā āvī. meṃ pahelī vār garbā karyā!
lines.en: It was great fun. I did garba for the first time!

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: રવિવારે હું આખો દિવસ સૂતી રહી. તમે શું કર્યું?
lines.roman: ravivāre huṃ ākho divas sūtī rahī. tame shuṃ karyuṃ?
lines.en: On Sunday I slept all day. What did you do?

lines.speaker: Bhavin
lines.native: અમે મૅચ જોઈ. પણ ભારત હારી ગયું.
lines.roman: ame mech joī. paṇ Bhārat hārī gayuṃ.
lines.en: We watched the match. But India lost.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: Oh no! I haven't seen the news.

lines.speaker: Bhavin
lines.native: કોઈ વાંધો નહીં. આવતી વખતે જીતીશું!
lines.roman: koī vāndho nahīṃ. āvtī vakhate jītīshuṃ!
lines.en: Never mind. We'll win next time!

culture: **તમે જમ્યા?** 'Have you eaten?' is as much a greeting of care as a real question in Gujarati homes. Gujarati weddings last several days, with a **ગરબા/દાંડિયા** night, **મહેંદી**, and the ceremony itself; guests are fed generously and gifts of cash (**ચાંલ્લો** *chāṃllo*) in round-plus-one amounts (₹501, ₹1101) are customary.
